about: CHAIN silver_road (Design/content/chains/silver_road.md): the road east to Aldeigjuborg and the silver of the Caliphate, from 797. Fourteen cards. A Svea trader at Dorestad pays with a coin that has writing and no face; the merchant follows it to Birka, learns the scale, sails east in company to the Volkhov, sees what the silver is paid for, and chooses. Four endings: the Svea keeps the road and the merchant is his sworn partner in the west (end_partner, as it really went); the merchant carries people east for silver (end_slaver, also as it really went); he buys a Frisian ship's boy out of the pen and takes him home (end_ransom, the honest road); he goes east without the Svea and sets a Frisian house on the Volkhov (end_frisian_house, history changed). Progress is flags ch_silver_road_1 to _10; the branch flags, the waits, the endings and the grand rewards are listed in the chain page. Cards with weight 0 are reached only by 'schedule' (their 'when' says when they belong). The spine's shared flags of the thread silver_road are set where its hooks say: sv_first_dirham, sv_scale, sv_moneyer_trusts. The words are in Data/writing/chain_silver_road.json; each option's note names the writing key of its outcome text (the engine shows the effects' own facts; the outcome keys are for the integrator). Nobody in these years says 'dirham' or 'Rus': the speech has 'the Saracens' silver', 'the writing silver', 'the east road', 'Aldeigja'. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Dorestad in the sailing months from 797, once the house has made three calls). A Svea trader pays on the scale with cut silver, and among it is a thin coin with writing on both sides and no king's head. Sources: men of Birka had been to Dorstadt (Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 27, of about 852; c. 20 for Catla's voyage); the oldest hoard at Staraya Ladoga closes with a coin of 786/7 and dirhams reach the Baltic about 800 (Noonan 1998; spine thread silver_road); a dirham weighs about 2.9 g, the new denier about 1.7 g (Frankfurt 794 c. 5, MGH Capit. I no. 28). That a dirham reached Dorestad as early as 797 is our invention (?). Cast: cast.holmfast, cast.sigimar. Sets ch_silver_road_1, the spine's sv_first_dirham, and on 'buy' sv_moneyer_trusts and ch_silver_road_has_coin.

cards.intention: A Svea trader pays for wine on a folding scale. Among his cut silver lies a thin broad coin with writing on both sides and no king's head. The moneyer has come down from the upper town to look at it.

cards.note: Step 2 (drawn at Birka in the market months, after step 1). Holmfast's booth: silver by weight, coin cut to make the weight and nicked to test it. Sources: folding scales and lead and bronze weights from graves and floors at Birka (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md; spine thread silver_road); Birka 'contained many rich merchants' (Rimbert c. 19). Dirhams at Birka from about 800. Cast: cast.holmfast. Sets ch_silver_road_2 and schedules step 3; 'scale' sets the spine's sv_scale.

cards.note: Step 3 (scheduled two days after step 2, at Birka). Holmfast goes east each summer and says what the east wants from the Rhine. Sources: the Rus bring beaver, black fox and swords to market (Ibn Khurradadhbih, about 846/885: of a later generation, used for what the road carried); Frankish blades in the north and the king's bans: no mail coat out of the realm (Herstal 779 c. 20), no arms to the Slavs and Avars and trade only at the named posts (Thionville 805 c. 7; chronicle_793.json 805-12-thionville-arms, 805-12-thionville-border-posts) (spine thread swords_north); glass beads and Rhine wine among what Birka wants (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md). From Birka to the Rus five days by sea (Adam of Bremen, scholion: LATER, about 1075, used for the distance only). Cast: cast.holmfast. Sets ch_silver_road_3, one of ch_silver_road_blades / ch_silver_road_lawful, and the timers ch_silver_road_wait_a (240 days: until next summer) and ch_silver_road_baltic (40 days: the sea card of step 4).

cards.intention: Holmfast is baling skins for the winter. He goes east when the ice lets go and comes back with the silver. He has been thinking about what a man from the Rhine could put in his ship.

options.label: Promise beads and wine, which no toll man will take your boat for

cards.note: Step 4, a side step (a sea card in the forty days after step 3, while she is likely still in the Baltic; if it never comes the chain goes on without it). A Gotland boat, low in the water with a chest nobody mentions, her steering oar gone off a lee shore. Sources: the spine's sea hook for silver_road; Gotland's silver: over 700 hoards, the men who sail east each summer (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md); the way to Birka beset by pirates (Rimbert c. 10). The skipper is Botmund (invented; a Gotland name of the rune stones, names_placeholder.json (?)). Sets ch_silver_road_4; 'help' sets ch_silver_road_gute_friend, which opens the cheap road at step 8.

cards.note: Step 5 (drawn at Birka early in the next summer, once the timer of step 3 has run out). Holmfast's ship is loading for the east and he takes the merchant in company. Sources: the sea road in: the gulf, the short strong river (the Neva) and the shallow rough lake (realms/rus.json road north 1-2; Adam of Bremen's sailing times: LATER); sea ships stop at Aldeigjuborg below the rapids of the Volkhov (peoples/baltic_east.md); ships go out in May and are home by autumn (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md). Cast: cast.holmfast. Sets ch_silver_road_5 and one of ch_silver_road_5_blades, _5_goods, _5_empty; every road teaches some Norse.

cards.note: Step 6, the first turn (drawn at Aldeigjuborg in the open months, after step 5). The landing on the Volkhov: skins and wax from the woods, silver from the south, and a dealer in the biggest house. Sources: Staraya Ladoga from 753 by its timbers, a smith's Norse tools in the oldest layer, dirhams from 786/7; no lord named before 839 ('deal with whoever sits in the biggest house': realms/rus.json who_holds); the trappers are the Finnic peoples round the lake, who later pay 'a squirrel-skin and a beaver-skin from each hearth' (Primary Chronicle 6367 = 859 (?)); silver weighed, cut and scratched: the Peterhof hoard, about 805, with marks in four scripts (chronicle_793.json 805-peterhof-hoard). The dealer is Vigmund (invented; Vig- + -mund, names_placeholder.json). Cast: cast.holmfast. Sets ch_silver_road_6, the spine's sv_first_dirham, one of ch_silver_road_6_blades / _6_goods / _6_tally, and schedules step 7.

cards.title: The landing at Aldeigja
cards.intention: The river is brown and fast and the sea ships go no further: above the town it breaks over rock. Log houses, a smithy, skins stacked like firewood, wax in cakes. Men from the woods stand apart with their bundles and speak a tongue nobody on your boat knows. In the biggest house a man named Vigmund weighs out thin silver with writing on it.

options.label: Sell him the four blades
options.note: outcome: chain_silver_road.s06.out_blades (the turn: about a hundred d over what the blades cost at home, and a timber of marten)

options.label: Sell him ten strings of beads
options.note: outcome: chain_silver_road.s06.out_beads (the men from the woods take beads before silver)

options.label: Sell him three casks of Rhine wine
Sell nothing; keep Holmfast's tally through the selling and take a hand's share

cards.note: Step 7, the heart of the chain (scheduled two days after step 6, at Aldeigjuborg). What the silver is paid for: people. Behind the dealer's house is a pen, and in it a Frisian ship's boy who can tally. Sources: slaves the chief thing the east road sells for silver (Ibn Rusta and Ibn Fadlan, 10th century: LATER, used for the trade and not quoted; peoples/baltic_east.md); Christians not to be sold out of the realm or to heathens (Herstal 779 c. 19; reputation_793.json sold_captives); the ransom of captives a Christian good work (Rimbert, Vita Anskarii c. 15 and 35: Anskar buys boys to teach them; Vita Rimberti c. 18: Rimbert gives his horse for a captive nun at Sliaswic; the chapter numbers were not re-checked tonight (?)); ships taken on the way to Birka (Rimbert c. 10). The boy is Folkbern (invented; Folk- + -bern), ship's boy of a Wijnaldum boat taken off the Danish coast. The price, a mark and two ounces (about 150 d of the new pennies), is our reckoning from later northern law, where a thrall is three marks (Västgötalagen: LATER) (?). Sets ch_silver_road_7, one of ch_silver_road_ransom / ch_silver_road_people / ch_silver_road_furs, and the timers ch_silver_road_wait_b (45 days: the way home) and ch_silver_road_wait_c (270 days: until next summer).

cards.note: Step 8 (drawn at Paviken on Gotland on any call after step 7; a branch, not a gate: the partner's ending does not need it). The Gotlanders go east each summer and put the silver under the floor; a shipwright offers to pilot the merchant east without the Svea. Sources: Paviken's shipwrights and smiths (ports_793.json); more silver found on Gotland than anywhere in the north, over 700 hoards, the Spillings hoard of 67 kg buried after 870 under a storehouse floor (peoples/svea_gotlandic.md; riddles_793.json rw_hoard_spillings); the spine's hook for Paviken. The 'skin in ten' the Svear are said to take for showing the way is invented (?). Botmund (invented). Sets ch_silver_road_8 and either ch_silver_road_own_road or ch_silver_road_keeps_faith.

cards.note: Step 9, the second turn (drawn at Dorestad once the way home has been sailed: the timer of step 7). The moneyer and a bag of the east's silver. Sources: Frankfurt 794 c. 5: the new pennies with the king's name to be taken everywhere (MGH Capit. I no. 28); a dirham about 2.9 g to the denier's 1.7, so twenty weigh as thirty-four; the coin's writing is the Saracens' and carries no image; Ibrahim ibn Yaqub saw dirhams of Samarkand at Mainz in 965 (chronicle_793.json 965-ibrahim-hedeby): that such silver reached a Rhine mint in the 800s is the chain's own turn. Cast: cast.sigimar. Sets ch_silver_road_9 and one of ch_silver_road_mint (which the changed-history ending asks for), ch_silver_road_keeps_whole, or neither; 'mint' and 'gift' set the spine's sv_moneyer_trusts.

cards.note: Step 10, a side step (a crew card at sea any time after step 6; the chain does not wait for it). The purse holds three kinds of silver and two of the crew argue about what the boat is worth. Sources: the spine's crew hook for silver_road (Ravn tests silver with a knife and his teeth and trusts no stamp; Aldger trusts the king's penny and nothing else); the three reckonings: the stamped penny (Frankfurt 794), weighed and nicked silver in the north, the east's coin by weight. Cast: cast.crew.ravn, cast.crew.aldger (if they are not aboard the forge gives two hands of their peoples, and the words still fit). Sets ch_silver_road_10; 'weigh' sets the spine's sv_scale.

cards.note: FINALE, ending end_partner: what really happened (drawn at Birka in the summer after step 7, for a house that has not gone east on its own and is not carrying people east). The Svea keeps the east road; the Frisian is his sworn partner in the west. Sources: the felag, the northern fellowship of one purse (the word is on 11th-century rune stones, the thing is older (?)); Birka men at Dorstadt and the traffic between them (Rimbert c. 20, 27); the eastern silver stayed in northern hands: the hoards of Gotland and Malaren against almost none on the Rhine before the 10th century (Noonan 1998). An oath on a ring is the heathen form (the Danes' oath to Alfred on the holy ring, Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 876: LATER, used for the custom). Cast: cast.holmfast. Sets ch_silver_road_end_partner and ch_silver_road_done; grand reward unlock_partner_holmfast (ring, cross) or unlock_factor_birka (bargain); 'ring' also sets ch_silver_road_ring_oath, which a priest at home may hear of.

cards.note: FINALE, ending end_frisian_house: history changed (drawn at Aldeigjuborg in the summer after step 7, for the house that took the Gotlander's pilotage at step 8). The merchant comes east without the Svea, and the dealer gives him ground for a house. What is real: no Frisian house on the Volkhov is known, and the east's silver stayed with the Svear, the Gotlanders and later the Rus; it is first seen on the Rhine in 965 (Ibrahim ibn Yaqub at Mainz). What is changed: a western house at the head of the road a century and a half early (changed_frisians_on_volkhov), and with 'mint' the east's silver into the pot at Dorestad in the lifetime of Charles (changed_dirhams_on_rhine). The pilot's words: the Neva, the lake crossed in the night calm, the twelve kilometres of river up to the town (realms/rus.json road north 1-2). Botmund and Vigmund are invented; cast.holmfast is wronged. Sets ch_silver_road_end_frisian_house and ch_silver_road_done; grand rewards unlock_plot_aldeigjuborg (every option) and on 'mint', the hardest road, unlock_pilot_volkhov as well; 'mint' and 'north' set the lasting cost ch_silver_road_holmfast_feud.
